title: Breaking Down on a Motorway
whatItIs: Breaking down on a motorway is dangerous because traffic passes very close and fast. Get yourself and your passengers away from it.
keyFacts: Never put a warning triangle on a motorway.
Don't try even simple repairs on the hard shoulder.
Marker posts on the hard shoulder show the direction of the nearest emergency phone.
If you have a disability that stops you leaving the car, stay in it with hazard lights on and call for help.
To rejoin, build up speed on the hard shoulder and move out only when there is a safe gap.

keyFacts.text: After stopping in an emergency area, you MUST use the emergency phone before you rejoin.

visual.caption: If you break down (with a hard shoulder)

items.title: Pull over
items.text: Get onto the hard shoulder and stop as far left as you can.

items.title: Lights on
items.text: Hazard lights on. Sidelights too at night or in poor visibility.

items.title: Get out on the left
items.text: Everyone out by the left-hand doors, away from the traffic.

items.title: Wait behind the barrier
items.text: Keep well away from your vehicle and the moving traffic.

items.title: Call for help
items.text: Use an emergency phone or your mobile and say where you are.

a.label: Ordinary road
points: If it is safe to place it

onTheTest.question: You break down on a motorway and stop on the hard shoulder. Where should you and your passengers wait?
options: Behind the barrier, away from the traffic
In the car, to keep warm and dry
On the hard shoulder behind the car
In front of the car to warn traffic
onTheTest.why: Get out by the left-hand doors and wait well away from the traffic, behind the barrier if there is one.

traps: No warning triangles on a motorway.
Leave the car by the left-hand doors, away from the traffic.
On a smart motorway with no hard shoulder, aim for an emergency area instead.
